title: Color Relay
premise: A neon-styled four-color board race where players roll a die, release tokens from base, circle a shared track, capture rivals, and race all pieces home first.
interaction_model: Turn-based tap/click input: press a dice button to roll, then tap one valid token on the canvas board to move it.
objective: Be the first color team to move all four tokens from base, around the shared loop, and into the final home lane.
progression: The match progresses through repeated four-player turns, with extra turns on rolling a 6, token unlocks from base, captures that reset rivals, and a final win state when one team gets all four tokens home.
theme: Futuristic neon relay race layered over a classic Ludo-style board game structure.
mood: Bright, arcade-like, competitive, celebratory, and easy to pick up.
likely_audience: players who enjoy simple local pass-and-play games
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core ruleset is a simplified Ludo/Parcheesi-style race game.
High confidence in the turn flow, capture rules, token release on 6, and win condition because these are explicit in code.
Moderate confidence that the intended play context is solo hot-seat or pass-and-play rather than online multiplayer, since no networking or AI is present.
Moderate confidence that the 'relay' theme is a presentation wrapper rather than a mechanical deviation from Ludo.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a polished browser game called "Color Relay," a mobile-friendly neon sci-fi reinterpretation of a classic four-color Ludo-style board race. Present the game full-screen with a glowing cosmic background, a central 15x15 board drawn on canvas, four colored teams (red, green, yellow, blue), and a compact HUD. Each team has four round tokens that begin in a colored home base. Players take turns in fixed order. On a turn, the active player taps a large dice button to roll; the die animates briefly and resolves to a value from 1 to 6. A token can only leave base when the player rolls a 6. Once on the board, tokens advance around a shared 52-space outer track, then enter that team's own 6-space home lane, and a token cannot move if the roll would overshoot its final destination. If a player lands on an opposing token on the shared track, that opponent is sent back to base, except on the four safe start squares where captures are not allowed. Rolling a 6 grants another turn. If no legal move exists after a roll, the turn skips automatically. The winner is the first team to get all four tokens fully home. Use touch/click controls so that after rolling, valid movable tokens are visually highlighted and the player taps one to move. Add a start overlay, a victory overlay, clear turn indicators, upbeat arcade sound effects for start, roll, move, capture, fail, and win, looping background music during play, a separate victory music loop after the match, and celebratory animated reaction media for captures and victory. Keep the presentation sleek, readable, responsive, and energetic, with glowing gradients, bold techno fonts, and an accessible casual-arcade feel.
